description: Kid-friendly astronomy paper reader where families browse simplified versions of real space research — homepage acts as a hub linking out to topic galaxies, a paper reader with a 'big words explained' helper, and a stargazing planner

pages.name: home
pages.description: Hub landing page that spokes out to topic areas, a featured paper, and reading tools
components: Top bar with the site mascot logo on the left, a row of nav links (Discover, Topics, Sky Tonight, Word Helper, For Grown-ups), and a 'Reading level' selector with three choices (Little Astronaut, Junior Scientist, Family Mode)

Hero hub block with a greeting headline, a one-sentence subtitle, and a circular arrangement of six spoke buttons (Planets, Stars, Galaxies, Black Holes, Rockets, Aliens?) each with an icon and a paper-count badge

Featured-paper card showing a telescope image, paper title rewritten for kids, the original author names with affiliations, a 'reading time' chip, an age-range chip, and a 'Start reading' primary button

Three-column 'Today in space' row with cards for Sky tonight (moon phase icon, visible planets list), Word of the day (term, kid-friendly definition, pronunciation), and Ask a scientist (question text, scientist name, photo, short answer preview)

Footer with columns for About, Schools, Parents & teachers, Original sources, plus a newsletter signup labeled 'Get a new space story every Sunday' and a credit line about partnering with real research archives

pages.name: topic
pages.description: Topic galaxy page listing every kid-translated paper in a chosen subject
components: Same top bar with the reading-level selector
Topic header with a back-to-hub link, a large topic title (e.g. 'Black Holes'), a friendly one-paragraph intro, and three stat chips (papers in this topic, newest update date, recommended ages)
Filter strip with chips for sub-topics (How they form, What's inside, Famous ones, Mysteries), a difficulty slider from 1 to 5 stars, and a sort dropdown (Newest, Easiest, Most loved)

Paper-card grid (three per row) where each card shows a thumbnail illustration, kid-title, original-title in smaller text below, a star-difficulty meter, reading-time chip, and a row of reaction emoji counts (mind-blown, curious, scary, cool)
Bottom 'Jump to another galaxy' strip with six small spoke buttons linking to the other topic pages

pages.name: paper
pages.description: Kid-friendly paper reader with a translated abstract, illustrated sections, and a vocabulary helper
components: Sticky reader top bar with back arrow, paper title, a progress bar showing how far through the paper the reader is, and toggle buttons for Read-aloud, Word Helper, and Original Version

Paper header card with the kid-title, original title and journal citation below it, author row with portrait avatars and institution names, publication date, and a 'Why this matters' callout box with one sentence

Main reading column split into four labeled sections (The Big Question, What They Did, What They Found, What It Means) where each section has a heading, a plain-language body, an inline illustration with caption, and underlined glossary words

Right-side Word Helper panel listing tricky terms from the paper — each entry shows the word, a one-sentence kid definition, a tiny diagram, and a 'say it' speaker button, plus a 'Show on the page' link that highlights the term in context

End-of-paper block with a three-question comprehension quiz (multiple choice with emoji answers), a reaction bar (mind-blown, curious, scary, cool buttons), and a 'Read the real grown-up version' link out to the source PDF

pages.name: sky-tonight
pages.description: Stargazing planner that connects what's visible in the sky to related papers
components: Same top bar
Location and time picker bar with a city input, a date picker defaulting to tonight, a time slider from sunset to sunrise, and a light-pollution indicator with a 1-to-9 scale

Sky-dome visualization panel showing a half-circle horizon view with labeled dots for visible planets, the moon at its current phase, and three featured constellations, plus a legend below mapping each dot to its name and brightness

'What you can see' list with rows for each visible object — each row has an icon, object name, best viewing time, naked-eye/binoculars/telescope indicator, and a 'Read about it' button linking to a related kid-paper
Family activity card at the bottom suggesting one stargazing activity for the night with a materials list, step-by-step numbered instructions, and a printable-version link

pages.name: for-grown-ups
pages.description: Parents and teachers page explaining the translation process and offering classroom tools
components: Same top bar

Intro section with a heading 'For parents, teachers, and curious grown-ups', a two-paragraph explanation of how real papers get translated, and a row of three credibility badges (Peer-reviewed sources, Reviewed by educators, Reviewed by scientists)
Three-step process diagram showing the pipeline from Original paper to Educator review to Kid-friendly version, with a portrait, name, and role under each step

Classroom tools section with a two-column layout — left column lists downloadable lesson plans (title, grade range, duration, download link), right column has a 'Build a reading list' tool with a search input and a saved-list preview area
FAQ accordion at the bottom with questions about reading levels, source accuracy, screen time, accessibility features, and how to suggest a paper for translation
